items.claim: A multistage login whose session is not bound to a specific username lets an attacker who triggers the second factor for their own login swap the session to another user's session and fully compromise that account.
items.body:
A multistage login whose session is not bound to a specific username lets an attacker who triggers the second factor for their own login swap the session to another user's session and fully compromise that account.

HackTricks reference: 21a66afe (notion:21a66afe-5662-40e3-86d5-0caa5622f188)
items.disproof: The multi-stage session state is re-bound to the username being authenticated, so a session that started for one account cannot be completed as another.

items.claim: User enumeration is proved by submitting the same password twice - once with a valid username and once with an invalid one - and diffing the two responses, since any observable difference discloses which usernames exist.
items.body:
User enumeration is proved by submitting the same password twice - once with a valid username and once with an invalid one - and diffing the two responses, since any observable difference discloses which usernames exist.

HackTricks reference: 21a66afe (notion:21a66afe-5662-40e3-86d5-0caa5622f188)
items.disproof: Both responses are byte-identical and take the same time regardless of whether the username exists, showing no user enumeration.

items.claim: A stay-logged-in (remember-me) cookie whose value is merely base64 of the username concatenated with an unsalted MD5 password hash is an insecure storage of credentials: anyone who steals the cookie can recover the plaintext password offline and reuse the login.
items.body:
A stay-logged-in (remember-me) cookie whose value is merely base64 of the username concatenated with an unsalted MD5 password hash is an insecure storage of credentials: anyone who steals the cookie can recover the plaintext password offline and reuse the login.

HackTricks reference: 2288404f (notion:2288404f-04b9-44f3-8fee-baa23830f5a5)
items.disproof: The remember-me value is an opaque, server-side-resolved random token with no username or password material embedded in it.
